lessons: Hover animations are gated behind `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`.
Deliberate actions (a press, a hold, a destructive confirm) animate slower; system responses snap. Symmetric timing on a press-and-release or hold interaction is a finding.

Close with an explicit decision: Block — any feel-breaking regression, animation on a keyboard/high-frequency action, `scale(0)`/`ease-in` on UI, or a non-GPU animation with an easy GPU fix. Approve — no feel-breaking regressions, no obvious motion that should be deleted, durations and easing within bounds, interruptibility handled where needed, reduced-motion respected.

lessons: Precise post search with paging (7/page): `https://section.blog.naver.com/ajax/SearchList.naver?countPerPage=7&currentPage=N&keyword=Q&orderBy=sim&type=post` + Referer `https://section.blog.naver.com/Search/Post.naver?keyword=Q`. Strip the `)]}',` prefix before json. Fields: `domainIdOrBlogId`, `logNo`, `title`, `contents`. Quoted keywords narrow results.
search.naver.com blog tab HTML gives only ~30 results and rewrites queries; cafe posts are mostly login-walled (skip).
Fetch `https://m.blog.naver.com/{id}/{logNo}` with an iPhone UA. Body starts at `class="post_ct` (works for SE2/SE3/SE-ONE).

Match the host with `(?:postfiles|blogfiles|mblogthumb-phinf|blogthumb|blogpfthumb-phinf)\.pstatic\.net/(Mj[^"'\\ ?]+)` — a `[a-z0-9]+\.pstatic` host pattern silently returns 0 images because the thumb hosts contain hyphens. The first image key of a post often 404s on `blogfiles` (it is the blog icon/thumbnail); skip failures, don't abort.
Posts fetched for TEXT (survey/evidence) need the same `post_ct` slice; strip `<script>` before tag-stripping or JS blobs pollute the text.
`data-width`/`data-height` in the HTML = uploaded original size; if <400 the original really is small (old mobile uploads are often 400px wide).

Search `<요리> 만들기` / `<요리> 레시피` / `"<정확한 이름>"` (2 pages each); recipe posts end with clean finished-plate shots, while `<요리> 후기`/brand searches return packaged retail goods and gift boxes. For a dessert with no hits under its exact name, try the generic form (`초코 구운찰떡`, `초코찰떡 오븐`).

Pull up to ~14 images per post (skip files <15 KB), one contact sheet per dish labelled `index:file widthpx`, then a second zoom sheet of the 10–20 finalists; pick finished food with no overlay text. A hand holding the food or a watermark is acceptable — the edit step removes it.
Keep `meta.json` {file → blog, logNo, url, key} while downloading; the chosen file's URL goes into the photo `sources.json` and the report.

Keyword phrasing decides recall: SearchList matches post prose, so search the words a poster would write (`다녀왔어요`, `허락받고 부착`, `설명회 X배너`), not topic nouns (`학원 포스터 학교` → mostly diaries). Run 10+ phrasings × 2–3 pages, dedupe on `blog/logNo` into a JSON file, then filter title+snippet with two regex groups (place AND object) before reading anything.
Titles can mislabel the field (e.g. a post titled 일식기능장 that is actually 복어기능장 material) - always look at the photos/documents.

lessons: **Verify before recommending**: Confirm something is unused before suggesting removal.
**Quantify impact**: Use estimated savings from insights. Don't prioritize changes with 0ms impact.
**Skip non-issues**: If render-blocking resources have 0ms estimated impact, note but don't recommend action.
**Be specific**: Say "compress hero.png (450KB) to WebP" not "optimize images".
**Prioritize ruthlessly**: A site with 200ms LCP and 0 CLS is already excellent—say so.

**Unused preconnects**: If flagged, verify by checking if ANY requests went to that origin. If zero requests, it's definitively unused—recommend removal. If requests exist but loaded late, the preconnect may still be valuable.
Key thresholds: TTFB < 800ms / < 1.8s / > 1.8s; FCP < 1.8s / < 3s / > 3s; TBT < 200ms / < 600ms / > 600ms; Speed Index < 3.4s / < 5.8s / > 5.8s

lessons: Hold at least two competing failure hypotheses at once, each with observed evidence for and against; a diagnosis that never named a rival hypothesis is a guess.
